newsitem.title: JAPAN: JVC to start DVD production in U.S. in April 1997.
newsitem.headline: JVC to start DVD production in U.S. in April 1997.

text.p: Victor Co of Japan Ltd (JVC) said on Tuesday that it would start production of digital video discs (DVDs) at JVC Disc America Co (JDC), its subsidiary in the United States, in April 1997.
DVDs will be produced at JDC's plants in Sacramento, California and Tuscaloosa, Alabama, the company said in a statement.
DVD is a new recording system which has large storage capacity and is expected to eventually make videocassette recorders, compact disc (CD) players and CD-ROMs obsolete.
JVC will start receiving orders for DVDs this month and begin sample shipments in November, JVC said.
JVC plans output of 600,000 discs per month, the company said.
A JVC spokesmen was not immediately available for comment on whether the company has already started DVD production in Japan or Europe.
